chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who took twenty-one pebbles and cast them, then one extra remained and he did not know which of them had been omitted, he said: “Let him return and cast one pebble at each one. And if a pebble falls from a man and he does not know which one it is, then let him take a pebble from beneath his feet and cast with it.”
He said: “If you cast a pebble and it falls into a litter, then repeat in its place. But if it strikes a person or a camel and then falls upon the Jimār, it suffices you.”

And he said regarding a man who cast at the Jimār, so he cast at the first with four pebbles, then cast at the last two with seven and seven: “He returns and casts three at the first, and he is done. And if he had cast at the middle with three, then cast at the last, then let him cast at the middle with seven. And if he had cast at the middle with four, he returns and casts three.”
He said: I said, “A man casts the Jimār in reverse order?” He said: “He repeats it for the middle one and Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.”

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it is sufficient and valid for fulfilling the requirement
key_terms.جَمْرَةِ ٱلْعَقَبَةِ: the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah, the last of the three stations
key_terms.حَصَاةً: a single pebble used for casting in the ritual of ramy
key_terms.مَحْمِلٍ: a litter or carried howdah into which a pebble may mistakenly fall
key_terms.ٱلْجِمَارِ: the pebble-throwing stations in Mina during hajj

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he makes a mistake while casting the pebbles at the Jimār during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for mistakes in the rite of casting pebbles during hajj, including uncertainty in the count, misdirected pebbles, and incorrect order. It clarifies how deficiencies are corrected so that the act of worship is completed properly.
